en: Homage be to Him who is the embodiment of compassion, who stands upon a lotus, whose lotus-feet are as beautiful as the red bandhūka flower, who holds a lotus in His hand, and who wears matted locks. (1)

Homage be to that Lord of Jinas, the Tathāgata, who was born in the land of Kāpūt, who is the embodiment of auspiciousness, who has reached the further shore of the ocean of the suffering of saṃsāra, and who consists of compassion. (2)
Homage be to you, Samantabhadra, worshipped by the gods, adorned with a golden necklace, bearing a crest-jewel upon your head, and consisting of the very essence of compassion. (3)

Homage be to him who is the very essence of beauty, who sits upon the bull-throne, who destroys the suffering of his devotees, who is the Tathāgata, who is adorned with precious jewels, and who consists of compassion. (4)

Homage be to him who is compassion itself, whose throat is adorned with six lines, who is captivating to the mind, whose wealth is worshipped by the three worlds, and whose lotus-heart is filled with mercy. || 5 ||
The wise Śaṅkhakarman composed this hymn on earth for the sake of merit;
those men who shall recite it with diligence have all gone to the delightful abode of the gods.
The Hymn to the Six States of Existence by the Glorious Noble Avalokiteśvara is completed.
